title: CEO Interview with Brendan Emery of iQ Sense - Semiwiki
gist: Brendan Emery of iQ Sense describes a battery-less, RFID-transponder-sized photonic integrated circuit implant that uses integrated waveguide interferometry for label-free, reagent-free continuous in vivo biochemical monitoring in animals, replacing drift-prone electrochemical sensing. The pitch is semiconductor platform economics applied to veterinary diagnostics: fix the hardware, grow the biomarker panel, start with companion animals, then extend to livestock, biosecurity and One Health surveillance.

themes.theme: Photonic sensing beats electrochemical for chronic implants

insights.claim: iQ Sense measures biochemistry optically on-chip using integrated waveguide interferometry in a photonic integrated circuit, deliberately rejecting electrochemical sensing because of its drift and consumable electrodes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Watch silicon photonics migrating from datacom into implantable biosensing — a new volume end-market for PIC foundries and packaging houses.
insights.quote: Rather than electrochemical sensing, with its drift and consumable electrodes, we measure biochemistry optically and on-chip using integrated waveguide interferometry.
insights.locator: The core is a photonic integrated circuit

insights.claim: For an implant that cannot be serviced after implantation, long-timescale measurement stability — not sensitivity or feature count — is the decisive engineering requirement.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Use post-implant stability, not lab accuracy, as the screening criterion when assessing any implantable-biosensor startup's technical claims.
insights.quote: for a device you can’t service after implantation, that stability is the whole game

insights.claim: The sensing approach is label-free and reagent-free, removing the recurring-consumable model that underpins conventional benchtop diagnostics.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Eliminating reagents shifts veterinary diagnostics revenue from razor-blade consumables toward hardware plus data subscriptions — a threat to incumbent analyser franchises.
insights.quote: It’s label-free, reagent-free, and stays stable over the timescales a chronic implant demands

themes.theme: Heterogeneous integration and packaging as the real moat

insights.claim: The hard part of the product is heterogeneous integration — co-packaging photonics, optoelectronics, low-power electronics, and wireless power and telemetry into one millimetre-scale volume — rather than any single novel device.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Value accrues to advanced-packaging and co-packaging capability; the defensibility of such startups sits in integration IP, not a sensor patent.
insights.quote: The interesting semiconductor work is in heterogeneous integration, co-packaging photonics, optoelectronics, low-power electronics and wireless power and telemetry

insights.claim: The implant is battery-less, wirelessly read, and targeted to fit within a volume on the scale of the RFID transponders pets already carry, making it a low-power and packaging problem more than a device problem.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Reusing the existing pet-microchip form factor lowers adoption friction and implies an addressable base of already-chipped animals rather than a greenfield market.
insights.quote: It’s battery-less and read wirelessly, so it’s as much a low-power and packaging challenge as a device one.

insights.claim: The category is newly feasible because photonic integration, mature flip-chip packaging, efficient energy harvesting, sub-milliwatt mixed-signal design and on-device AI all matured in parallel — none of them individually novel.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A convergence-timing thesis: the same five matured building blocks unlock a wave of implantable and ambient sensing nodes, expanding demand for sub-mW analog and PIC content.
insights.quote: None is individually novel, co-integrating them into an implantable sensing node is what’s newly feasible.
insights.locator: The timing works because of convergence

insights.claim: iQ Sense's architecture holds the hardware platform fixed while expanding the panel of biomarkers it addresses, explicitly importing the semiconductor pattern of building a platform once and amortising it across many products.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: If it works, gross margin expands with each added marker at near-zero incremental hardware cost — the key metric to track is markers per platform generation.
insights.quote: the platform stays fixed while the panel of markers it addresses grows

insights.claim: The company frames the opportunity as creating a new category — 'Continuous Biological Visibility' — positioned as a foundational data layer of animal healthcare rather than as another wearable product.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Category-creation framing means the near-term risk is market education and reimbursement-equivalent buy-in from vets, not technical failure.
insights.quote: We think continuous biological visibility becomes a foundational layer of animal healthcare, and the platform economics of silicon are what put it in reach.
insights.locator: Our first applications are in companion animals

insights.claim: The stated gap being attacked is that animal healthcare runs on snapshots — periodic blood tests and exams — with everything in between unmeasured, and that most diseases develop continuously while being managed with intermittent data.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The same continuous-versus-intermittent-data argument that repriced human CGM companies is now being pointed at veterinary diagnostics incumbents.
insights.quote: Most diseases develop continuously, but we’re trying to manage them using intermittent data.
insights.locator: Animal healthcare still runs on snapshots

themes.theme: Go-to-market sequencing and One Health optionality

insights.claim: Companion animals are the deliberate first market because chronic diseases there already require ongoing management, creating existing willingness to pay for continuous monitoring before the platform expands to equine, livestock, biosecurity and One Health.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Sequencing by fastest value demonstration rather than by species size is the standard deep-tech beachhead play — judge progress by paid pet-clinic pilots, not livestock TAM slides.
insights.quote: Our roadmap isn’t organised around species. It’s organised around demonstrating the platform where it creates value fastest, then applying the same underlying technology to increasingly larger opportunities.
insights.locator: Every platform technology needs an initial application

insights.claim: In livestock, continuous in vivo monitoring is pitched as infrastructure for earlier infectious-disease detection, biosecurity, antimicrobial stewardship and population-level health surveillance — a policy-adjacent demand pool beyond pet owners.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Government and agri-policy budgets for AMR and zoonotic surveillance are a potential non-consumer funding channel; watch for grant or public-programme contracts as validation.
insights.quote: improve biosecurity, strengthen antimicrobial stewardship, and provide new tools for population-level health surveillance

insights.claim: The full system pairs an implanted biochemical sensor with an external reader capturing heart rate, respiratory rate, movement and behaviour, with AI interpreting the longitudinal dataset rather than isolated measurements.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The defensible asset over time is the longitudinal multimodal animal dataset — a data moat that compounds with installed base, not the chip itself.
insights.quote: AI then helps interpret those longitudinal datasets, identifying meaningful biological changes over time rather than relying on isolated measurements.
insights.locator: The implantable sensing platform continuously measures

insights.claim: iQ Sense argues lab validation only proves individual technologies work, whereas in vivo validation is the only test of whether implant communications, optical stability, wireless power transfer, cloud analytics and AI function as one system.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Treat lab-only milestone announcements from implantable-sensor startups as low-information; the de-risking event is multi-month in-animal system data.
insights.quote:
Laboratory validation demonstrates that individual technologies work.
In vivo validation demonstrates that the complete system works.

insights.claim: The company is at the stage of completing a commercial MVP alongside in vivo validation in pets and livestock, and is still recruiting veterinary practices, breeders and animal health pharmaceutical companies into validation studies and pilots.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Pre-revenue, pre-pilot stage: any exposure here is venture-risk, and the near-term catalysts are named pharma or clinic partnerships.
insights.quote: As we progress through commercial MVP completion and in vivo validation, we’re looking to expand those collaborations.

insights.claim: The founding team pairs 25+ years of animal health commercial leadership at Boehringer Ingelheim and Norbrook Laboratories with two decades of semiconductor and photonic development at ASML and imec.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Cross-domain founder pairing (deep semiconductor plus incumbent-channel commercial) is the credible-team signal for a category that needs both fab access and vet distribution.
insights.quote: my co-founder and CTO, Madhu Jambunathan, spent two decades developing advanced semiconductor and photonic technologies at organisations including ASML and imec
insights.locator: The company was really born from combining

insights.claim: iQ Sense joined Silicon Catalyst's 12-month ChipStart AU programme specifically for semiconductor-focused mentoring spanning manufacturing, packaging and commercialisation, arguing that for deep-tech chip startups commercialisation is half the challenge.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Silicon Catalyst's accelerator pipeline is a useful early-look funnel for pre-seed semiconductor deal flow outside the usual US/EU clusters.
insights.quote: developing the technology is only half the challenge. Successfully commercialising it is equally important
insights.locator: Why did you join Silicon Catalyst ChipStart AU
